ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint/trigger: 5-day history of dry cough and continuously streaming nose; no specific trigger or exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline/progression: Abrupt onset 5 days ago; cough every 20–30 min, currently dry; nasal discharge described as “pretty green.” Brief self-limited diarrhoea at onset; subjective fever with alternating chills. Symptoms partially relieved by 2–3 sachets/day of Lemsip.
- ENT-related symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling: Denied.  
  • Nasal/ocular: Constant rhinorrhoea; no epistaxis; denies itchy/watery eyes.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: Denied.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: Denied.  
  • Neck pain/swelling: Denied.
- Relevant past episodes/treatments: None for similar illness; no prior antibiotics or ED visits for current episode.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies; mild seasonal hay-fever.
- Current medications:  
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Lisinopril – patient believes “200” (likely 20 mg) once daily.  
  • Lemsip (paracetamol-containing cold remedy) 2–3 times daily PRN.  
  • No rescue inhalers or auto-injectors.
- Social context: Lives with partner and dog; office manager; non-smoker; drinks “odd sherry.”

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: No dyspnea, stridor, or increased work of breathing reported.
- Mental status/associated features: Alert; reports myalgias, subjective fever/chills.
- Vitals & exam findings: Not recorded (remote video consult).
- Accompaniment: Patient at home; partner present in household (not on call).

Assessment:
Working impression: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold or influenza-like illness) in patient with type 2 diabetes and hypertension.
Evidence: 5-day abrupt onset of dry cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, subjective fever; no dyspnea or focal chest pain; infection typically self-limiting.
DDx (ranked, aligned with transcript):
1. Acute viral URI – High likelihood; classic symptom cluster and time-course, no concerning chest findings.
2. COVID-19 infection – Medium likelihood; overlapping symptoms and pandemic prevalence; no anosmia/dyspnea but should be considered. 
3. Acute bacterial sinusitis (post-viral) – Medium; green nasal discharge and >5 days duration, but lacks facial pain/tenderness and fever documentation.
No conflict noted between transcript and above DDx items.

Plan:
- Symptomatic care: Continue Lemsip up to recommended doses; avoid additional paracetamol products.
- Monitoring:
  • Purchase thermometer; check temperature regularly.  
  • Maintain hydration and rest.
- Red-flag / escalation advice:
  • Seek medical review if temperature ≥ 37.5–38 °C persists or spikes, cough worsens, develops purulent sputum, haemoptysis, shortness of breath, chest pain, or nasal bleeding.  
  • If severe breathing difficulty or sudden deterioration, call emergency services (999/EMS).
- Follow-up:
  • Re-consult GP/ENT if symptoms persist >10–14 days or red-flags occur; antibiotics may be considered if bacterial infection suspected.  
  • Ensure routine diabetes and blood-pressure reviews with GP; discuss home blood-glucose monitoring at next appointment.  
  • Consider COVID-19 testing per local guidance if fever develops or exposure risk increases.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: objective vital signs (temperature, HR, BP, SpO₂); physical ENT and chest examination; precise medication doses; home blood-glucose readings; COVID-19 testing status; vaccination status; history of influenza vaccination.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none significant.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor omissions but clinically adequate.
